title: I built a horror game with Claude Code + ChatGPT where the house AI rebuilt a dead mom's voice. At 3:15 AM it plays YOUR voice back.
author: Happy_Literature_194
selftext:
Two weeks ago I posted Night One here (you play the smart home, something outside copies the family's voices). It got 22K views and your comments basically wrote my to-do list. Here's the follow-up, and what I learned building it.

Wake Word: Almost Home. Sarah died a year ago. Ember, the house AI, kept every word she ever said, and tonight it is keeping her last promise: "I'll be home." One person in the family isn't who they say they are. You have until dawn to find out who, using nine cameras, infrared and a notebook Ember can't read. Four endings, a different culprit each run, about 20 minutes.

How I built it:  
\- I wrote a full design doc with Claude, then gave it to ChatGPT to tear apart. That second opinion caught unfair clues and endings that didn't follow from what the player did.  
\- Claude Code built it in batches, each in a fresh session, with a short CLAUDE.md that maps the project. That saved a lot of usage.  
\- Images were the hardest part. I made the rooms and the family in ChatGPT and placed the characters in code. You can still spot it in places. Next time I'll generate each room with the person already in it.  
\- The best thing I did was make Claude Code play the game with real clicks, including one run at real speed. That run found a bug the fast runs never could: a name clash had silently killed every ambient house sound.  
\- The trailer is real game footage recorded by Claude Code, with an ElevenLabs narrator.

The microphone is optional. The game records you saying the wake word, and later the house plays your own voice back. It all stays in your browser, nothing is uploaded.

The game is free. There's an optional $1-4 supporter pack (piano lullaby, wallpapers, a story booklet and the soundtrack).

Play it here: https://redrakam.itch.io/wake-word-almost-home

If you play, tell me which ending you got and who you suspected first. And if you've found a better way to put AI characters into AI backgrounds, I'd love to hear it.
